hero.description: Kayaking the Nam Song is the active way to move through Vang Vieng's defining landscape: the river keeps you inside the valley while limestone walls and rural banks change slowly around you.

chapters.label: THE RIVER
chapters.title: Vang Vieng looks different when the road disappears
chapters.body: On the Nam Song, the karst is no longer a backdrop behind scooters and fields. The river creates a continuous line through the valley, which is why kayaking feels more like moving through the landscape than visiting a single attraction.

chapters.label: THE CONTROL
chapters.title: Choose kayaking when you want to participate
chapters.body: Tubing lets the river set most of the pace; kayaking gives you more control and more work. That makes it the stronger choice for visitors who want an active half-day rather than a long float.

note.label: USEFUL CHOICE
note.text: Kayak for movement and control. Tube when the point is to slow down.

chapters.label: OPERATOR
chapters.title: The briefing matters more than the sales board
chapters.body: Ask what the trip includes, where it starts and ends, how current water levels affect the route, and whether a guide stays with the group. A clear safety briefing is a better quality signal than an overloaded package of extra stops.

beforeYouLeave.title: Pack for a river, not for a photo stop
beforeYouLeave.body: Use footwear that can get wet, sun protection, a secure dry bag and as little loose gear as possible. Keep the camera decision secondary to staying comfortable in the boat.

note.label: RIVER RULE
note.text: Life jacket on · valuables sealed · follow the guide.

items.label: Time
items.detail: Allow for pickup or transfer, safety briefing, paddling and return logistics.

items.label: Conditions
items.detail: Ask the operator how the current river affects difficulty and duration.

items.label: Safety
items.detail: Use proper flotation and follow the guide's line in faster sections.

items.label: Gear
items.detail: Assume everything not sealed can get wet.

faq.question: Is kayaking the Nam Song difficult?
faq.answer: Difficulty depends on the section and current water level. Ask the operator what the route is like that day rather than relying on a generic rating.

faq.question: How long does a kayaking trip take?
faq.answer: A half-day is the most useful planning window once transport, briefing and river time are included.

faq.question: Kayaking or tubing in Vang Vieng?
faq.answer: Choose kayaking for an active, controlled river experience; choose tubing for a slower float with less paddling.

faq.question: What should I bring?
faq.answer: Sun protection, water-friendly footwear and a proper dry bag. Keep valuables minimal and use the supplied life jacket.

faq.question: Can beginners kayak the Nam Song?
faq.answer: Many trips are designed for visitors without advanced experience, but suitability depends on the day's water level and route. Ask the operator before booking.
